newsitem.title: UK: Insurers gain on continued bid speculation.
newsitem.headline: Insurers gain on continued bid speculation.

text.p: Shares in insurers Prudential Corp Plc and Commercial Union Plc moved higher on Thursday as bid speculation centring on the financial services industry lent support, analysts said.
Prudential had added 13p to 504 at 1320 GMT, while Commercial Union was 17-1/2p higher at 687p.

One analyst said that no-one wanted to sell Prudential shares because of ongoing speculation that the company, which specialises in life insurance, might join forces with banking and financial services group Abbey National Plc.
Abbey National shares shed 5 1/2p to 701p. following a strong run over recent weeks.

Commercial Union extended Wednesday's 9 1/2p gains as the market chewed over press reports of a possible tie-up with the financial services business of B.A.T. Industries. B.A.T. shares added 3p to 472 1/2p.

Press reports on Wednesday said that B.A.T. had considered merging its financial services arm, consisting mainly of general and life insurance companies, with a quoted composite insurer. They highlighted CU as the putative partner but said the proposals had floundered.
Prudential led the gainers among life insurers but Legal & General Group also rose, adding 4 1/2p to 359 1/2 while Sun Life & Provincial firmed 4p to 259 1/2.
Among the composites, General Accident added 8p to 734, Royal & Sun Alliance gained 10p to 461 1/2 and Guardian Royal firmed 8 1/2p to 274 1/2p.
